deep.reconstruction:
This page has no running text. It is a sheet of recycled fan-fold computer paper. The printed part is a JES2 job-end banner: 'CRAY6', 'END JOB 13 ... 3.24.18 PM 19 AUG 82'. Over it Grothendieck drew about 25 hand sketches in pencil, black ink and coloured felt-tip.

Each main sketch is a circle with arcs crossing it from one boundary point to another. These are pseudo-line arrangements in the standard disc model of the real projective plane: boundary points are identified antipodally, and each pseudo-line is a chord or arc joining antipodal points.

What the sketches show:
- Many cells are labelled with small numerals, mostly 3 and 4, some 5, and one large 6. These record how many sides each cell has (triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons). This is the usual bookkeeping for simple arrangements: for n lines, the cell count f2 is n(n-1)/2+1 and the side counts sum to 2n(n-1). It is also the bookkeeping behind Levi's bound of at least n triangles.
- Some boundary arcs are thickened in green or black. These seem to mark distinguished boundary segments, perhaps the 'murs' (walls) or zones bounded by a chosen pseudo-line. That fits the following page, which defines 'fuseaux' (spindles) bounded by two pseudo-lines D, D'.
- The yellow/red/black pentagram sketch (top left) is the 5-line arrangement with its central pentagon and five triangles; a hatched triangle is marked.
- The 12-spoke diagram (bottom right) is a non-simple pencil of lines through one point. This is the extreme 'critical' degenerate position.
- Several sketches contain wavy pseudo-lines. Most likely these show a curve D being moved through an arrangement, sweeping across vertices.
- The isolated hexagons and pentagons probably sketch individual cells. The boundary numbering 1, 2, 4, 11, 12, 13 around one green disc labels boundary points or pseudo-lines.

Place in the dossier: the previous page studies the 'surface cellulaire des positions relatives' X* = Bal(Σ). This is a 2-dimensional cell complex built from an arrangement Σ:
- its vertices are critical relative positions of an added pseudo-line D;
- its edges are sub-stable positions;
- its faces are stable positions.
The next page classifies 'fuseaux' (cellular, semi-cellular, ordinary) according to which of the two bounding walls are super-critical. It conjectures a one-to-one correspondence between fuseaux and isotopy classes of sub-stable positions.

In modern language, X* is essentially the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid. That space is the poset/cell complex of single-element extensions, i.e. of the ways to add one more pseudo-line. This page is the experimental side of that study: hand enumeration of cell structures and of positions of a new pseudo-line, to test the local description of X* near vertices, edges and faces.
errors: Nothing on this page can be checked as an assertion; it is purely exploratory drawing. Some sketches are not simple arrangements (pencil through a point, wavy curves crossing more than once?), presumably on purpose, to depict critical or degenerate positions. Whether every drawn curve meets every other exactly once cannot be verified at this resolution.

ideas.what: Disc model of the projective plane with pseudo-line arrangements; labelling cells by their number of sides
ideas.modern_name: Simple pseudoline arrangements / face-vector (p-vector) of arrangements; triangle counting (Levi, Grünbaum)

ideas.what: Moving an additional pseudo-line D through an arrangement Σ; distinguishing critical (vertex), sub-stable (edge) and stable (face) positions. Together these form a 2-dimensional cell complex X* (from the context pages)
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (single-element extensions); related to the Generalized Baues Problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sturmfels & Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); Las Vergnas (single-element extensions); Mnëv–Ziegler

ideas.what: Degenerate central arrangement (pencil of 12 lines through one point) drawn alongside simple arrangements

missed.claim: These drawings are the experimental side of Grothendieck's construction of a cell 'surface' X* = Bal(Σ) of relative positions of a new pseudo-line with respect to an arrangement. That object is, in effect, the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid. Calling it a 'surface' implicitly expects it to be a 2-manifold or sphere-like complex. Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) studied this ten years later, and its homotopy type in general rank is tied to the Generalized Baues Problem. Grothendieck's 1983-84 work on it, including the classification of 'fuseaux' on the next page, does not appear in that literature.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and possibly a different, explicit local cell-description (vertices, edges, fuseaux) of rank-3 extension spaces. This could be compared with the Sturmfels–Ziegler results.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is pure exploratory sketching of projective pseudo-line arrangements, with cell side-counts, on a 1982 Cray printout. Its only interest comes from the surrounding pages, which anticipate the extension-space viewpoint. The page itself contains no statement.
transcription_corrections: The cell labels written like 'ε' are reversed-looking 3's, and the 'h'-like glyphs are 4's; a few cells are labelled 5, and one bold '6' appears in the right-middle-lower disc.
There is a 12-spoke pencil diagram (bottom right) and a pentagram 5-line arrangement with hatched triangle (top left), drawn in yellow, dark red and black ink.
The vertical '8 2 1' near top centre is pencil and may be a scribble or tally rather than numbers attached to a figure.
The archive page number '151' is pencilled at the bottom left margin.
